_comment: The Phase 1 cross-host parity gate, as data. Both hosts and all three tools read
this file, so a gate re-run cannot silently use different exclusions from the run
that established the baseline — which is exactly the risk when Phase 4 touches the
composite pass and someone re-runs the gate from memory of the flags.
Run it with:  node tools/parity-gate.mjs --mode a
Each entry in `exclude` removes a term from the render. They are NOT convenience
switches: every one is a term that cannot agree between two GL implementations by
construction, and each is justified by a measurement recorded in `why`. Adding to
this list weakens the gate. Do not add to it without a measurement, and record the
See README 'Cross-host parity gate' for the full rationale and results, and
CONTRACTS.md 'Rejected approaches' for what was tried and abandoned.

feedback.why: Each frame warps the previous frame's buffer, so any difference is fed back and amplified. Two hosts running byte-identical shaders diverge over a 20 s run by design.

grain.why: composite.frag adds hash12(vUv * vec2(1913,1487) + fract(F_TIME*3.7)*137), a fract chain chaotic in the last bit of its input. An FMA contracted one way by the D3D compiler and another by the GL driver decorrelates it completely. Measured: leaving grain in scores 0.8634 mean, because with feedback cleared a fresh frame is 97.8% black at mean luma 3.7/255 and SSIM then measures 8-bit quantization noise.

particles.why: The particle layer is GL_POINTS. ANGLE expands sized points to quads on D3D11 where desktop GL rasterizes them natively, so sub-pixel coverage differs. Measured: leaving particles in scores 0.9948 mean / 0.9425 min, and every failing frame's amplified diff is pure particle speckle with no structural difference.

a.name: strict
a.description: The real gate. Every term that cannot agree by construction is removed, so the diff measures shader math. A failure here is a genuine contract bug: diagnose it, do not threshold it away.

b.name: informational
b.description: Full feedback over the whole timeline. Not a pass/fail on drift; the point is the shape of the curve, because a cliff means a real bug hiding behind expected divergence.

baseline.note: Curve is flat rather than decaying: 0.97-0.999 band over 20 s, so the feedback loop is contractive. era-brent misses the frame-60 check at 0.9155 — most particle-dominated preset, highest-contrast palette.

timelines.why: 20 s off the synthetic driver at seed 0x5F356495. General-purpose coverage: onsets, beat sweep at 112 BPM, bass modulation, chord changes.
Constructed, not recorded. Fires novelty deliberately so the novelty->fractalMorph and novelty->feedbackDecay mappings are exercised; the primary timeline never fires one.
